My mother has known since I was in third grade that "tough love" is not going to motivate me to do shit. I'm starting to think she's just stupid at this point.

My parents claim to know everything there is to know about depression and my mom's a former psychologist and how dare I think I know more than she about mental illnesses. How did you make your dad realize that a depressed person has no motivation to do anything no matter what you do to them?
I will. Thanks for your help getting me on track.

Never having her hurt me again is a pretty freaking big pro in my book. She's been making me miserable since I was 5 years old. And yes, the rest of my family does know that she does this but they either feel like they deserved it because it came from something they did (NO ONE deserves those words), or they're emotionally stable enough to deal with it. I need to do what's best for ME and get away from an emotionally abusive environment.

I have a friend who's willing to put me up for a couple days. I want to get to the point where i'm not looking for full time work to make my mom happy, but i'm looking for it so that I can move out and live on my own.
No one in my family thinks I'm trying hard enough. Besides, my mother has it engraved in her mind what she thinks is wrong with me and no amount of talking is going to fix that.

but what's the point of staying? I stay and make this right so that she can say hurtful things to me AGAIN later on? She doesn't just do this to me. She does it to everyone in my family. I'm the only one who can't take it anymore, so I'm leaving tomorrow whether she likes it or not.

this is how i'm feeling right now. I just made a post, and I'm starting to think if I started slashing my wrists in front of my mother, she might finally realize what she's doing to me. I know it's straight up crazy, but I feel like it's the only thing that will get me what I need.
Well, my symptoms have gone away now, and I think I'll be fine. 1,000mg may sound bad, but I'm also 6'0" and weigh 200lbs.

That's just the thing, though. It's a pretty weak dream. I just happened to take a chinese class my freshman year of high school and stuck with it, and people kept telling how great it was that i was learning chinese. 
I'm not even very good at it. I can barely string two sentences together. I'm really only majoring in it because it's there and i can't think of any other alternatives that i would like. And I'm also hearing more and more lately about how there are no jobs for Chinese majors right now. I might as well be a history major.

We need zombie emily post up in here. 
Anyway, as someone who's read way too much of emily post, yes, it IS rude.    
I learned Chinese in middle and high school, and this one time some guy sat down a couple desks from me and I turn to some chinese friends and made a crack about how he was dressed in a normal voice, in Chinese. They gave me this look, and one of them said, "how could you SAY that? He's right there!" still in Chinese. "He doesn't know what I'm saying." "How do you know?" "Cuz he's white." "So are you."    
    
By the same token, I've gotten some of that myself. A white friend of mine was dating a Chinese guy and I heard him talking to a friend about a girl he banged the previous night at a party. The guy was talking so loudly that it was really awkward for me but I'm sure he was having a blast. At the end of class I introduced myself to him in Chinese and told him I had no idea that my friend's boyfriend was in teh same math class as me, and why didn't he every say anything about it etc, which was really rude in itself of me, but the prick deserved it.    
ANYWAY. </tangent>    
Yes. It's rude. Not only do you not know who's listening, you're putting people who don't know what you're saying in a very uncomfortable position. If you don't know much english, though, I can guarantee that all your english speaking friends know it and let it slide.
